newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs to borrow $200-250 mln on intl market-PM.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs to borrow $200-250 mln on intl market-PM.

text.p: Kazakhstan plans to raise the equivalent of $200-250 million on international markets this autumn to help resolve some of its current social problems, Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Wednesday.

"The government is planning this loan, and therefore we are watching the rates of the yen, mark and the dollar on foreign markets. The borrowing will be no less than $200-250 million, and this will probably happen in autumn," Kazhegeldin said.

Kazhegeldin said the loan would help pay off by January 1 huge debts to Kazakh pensioners which total around $500 million. "We propose to make payments to today's pensioners at the expense of future generations and the future economy," he said.

The premier said the borrowing would not be burdersome for Kazakhstan's current economy. "Realistically, Kazakhstan can borrow today even $1 billion -- such are the offers from finance companies," he said, but added the oil-rich former Soviet republic would only cautiously build up its debt.

He said the government expected the borrowing would be preceeded by a higher credit rating for sovereign debt from international rating agencies. Last year Moody's gave assigned Kazakhstan a Ba3 sovereign ceiling for long-term foreign-currency bonds. Agencies IBCA and Standard and Poor's both gave BB-.

Last December the Central Asian state tapped international markets with its debut $200-million Eurobond, which was snapped up by investors. The three-year bond, organised by Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, was priced to yield 9.3 percent or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes.
